mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the empty set (∅) is incorrect?

options.B: It is a subset of every set.

mcqs.explanation: The empty set has no elements, so its cardinality is zero and it is a subset of every set. Statement C claims that the empty set has exactly one element, which is false; therefore C is the incorrect statement.

mcqs.question: A set S has exactly five distinct elements. Which of the following statements is always true?

options.C: S is a subset of the empty set.
options.D: S contains the empty set as an element.

mcqs.explanation: A set with five distinct elements has a finite number of members; its cardinality (size) is 5. Hence statement A is always true. The other options are false: a set with five elements is not infinite, cannot be a subset of the empty set, and need not contain the empty set as an element.

mcqs.question: Consider the sets N = {1,2,3,…} and Z = {…, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2,…}. Which of the following correctly compares their sizes?

options.A: Both N and Z are infinite and have the same cardinality.
options.B: N is a proper subset of Z and has a smaller cardinality.
options.C: Z is a proper subset of N and has a larger cardinality.
options.D: Both N and Z are finite sets.

mcqs.answer: Both N and Z are infinite and have the same cardinality.
mcqs.explanation: Both the set of natural numbers (N) and the set of integers (Z) are countably infinite; there exists a one‑to‑one correspondence between them, so they have the same cardinality. Therefore option A is correct, while B and C incorrectly claim a size difference, and D is false because both sets are infinite.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets is a singleton set?
mcqs.explanation: A singleton set contains exactly one element. Among the options, only {7} has a single element, making option C the correct choice. Option A is the empty set (no elements), B has two elements, and D has three elements.
